executive_summary: MStar US Equity enters the October 26 review with four live tensions that together define the fund's active posture. The SMID/value tilt — expressed through +2.30 pts in United States Sml Growth, +2.66 pts in United States Mid Value, and a linked +2.20 pts in Industrials — is the dominant theme, but each exposure carries a different signal configuration and a different research support status. United States Sml Growth has no live thesis on record and no matched sector research; the +2.30 pt overweight is driven entirely by the Wasatch sleeve with the STF negative at -2.15% and only the algo weakly agreeing at +0.23 pts. United States Mid Value is the strongest-signalled of the three style bets — STF ranks #2 of 9 in US styles and sits at its 12-month high — but no current research underwrites it. Industrials is the most structurally problematic: both model layers disagree (STF -3.28%, algo active weight -2.56 pts relative to benchmark), the only live thesis is a placeholder for tracking purposes, and the internal research is from a May 2025 deck. Financials (+1.66 pts) is overweight with both layers pointing underweight, but internal research notes select value in capital markets and asset managers. MTD active return was -1.56%, with overweight positions costing -1.92%, underscoring the urgency of refreshing the underwriting for each off-signal bet.

key_insights.label: SMID overweight is a multi-sleeve aggregate, not a single approved bet
key_insights.insight: The fund's combined SMID tilt — across United States Sml Growth (+2.30 pts), United States Mid Value (+2.66 pts), and a related Industrials sector overweight (+2.20 pts) — is the emergent sum of Wasatch, MFS, Opportunistic, and Systematic SMID sleeves, none of which individually approved the aggregate fund-level style expression.
key_insights.why_it_matters: This means no single manager is monitoring the combined size-factor risk, which contributes 4.02% of active variance in Size and 22.19% in Market Sensitivity — the fund's largest style risk drivers.

key_insights.label: United States Mid Value is the most signal-supported overweight but has no live research
key_insights.insight: At STF -0.54% and ranked #2 of 9 in US styles (at the top of its own 12-month range), United States Mid Value has the best relative model signal of the four challenge positions, yet no matched research deck exists to underwrite the thesis at the holding level.
key_insights.why_it_matters: Without documentation, the IC cannot distinguish between deliberate value rotation conviction and implementation drift from the MFS sleeve, which carries Cigna (+0.41 pts active), Duke Energy (+0.33 pts), and Travelers (+0.24 pts) entirely without benchmark offset.

key_insights.label: Industrials overweight is explicitly diverging — both model layers point underweight
key_insights.insight: With STF -3.28% (ranked #10 of 11 in US sectors) and algo active weight -2.56 pts relative to benchmark, Industrials is the only challenge position where both layers are aligned against the overweight. The live thesis is a placeholder, and the sector research (May 2025 neutral stance) is over 16 months stale.
key_insights.why_it_matters: The fund continues to hold +2.20 pts in a sector where the model disagrees at both levels, overweight positions cost -1.92% MTD, and no fresh underwriting exists — this is the highest-priority documentation or defend-or-resize decision this cycle.

Without a thesis, there is no falsification condition, and the STF has been negative throughout the past 12 months (range: -3.53% to -1.73%), meaning the position has never had model support over that window.

The algo active weight (relative to benchmark) is +0.23 pts, providing weak agreement. The partial alignment means the sizing cannot be defended on model grounds alone; the improvement trend is encouraging but the STF has not crossed zero in 12 months.
challenge_brief.relative_signal_readthrough: At -2.15%, the STF ranks #5 of 9 in US styles — exactly at the universe median — while the universe is not uniformly negative (United States Sml Value is +0.39%). Sitting at the median offers no relative preference argument. Separately, the current STF is at the 82nd percentile of its own 12-month range (history: -3.53% to -1.73%), meaning this is near the best the signal has been in a year — but the bar is entirely negative, so this is a regime-depressed winner context, not an attractive absolute read.
challenge_brief.vir_decomposition_readthrough: The STF decomposition shows growth (+4.60%) and yield (+1.56%) as positive contributors, but valuation_adjustment_top_down at -4.00% and currency at -1.68% are the main drags. challenge_brief.market_context_readthrough: The only available approved-source evidence is a FactSet Earnings Insight dated May 29, 2026 — four months stale — which covers broad S&P 500 earnings beats led by Magnificent 7 and Communication Services. This data has no small-cap growth-specific read and should not be used to support the position. No current approved-source research covers US small-cap growth specifically.
challenge_brief.measured_risk_readthrough: Market Sensitivity accounts for 22.19% of active variance — the fund's largest style risk driver — and the Sml Growth overweight is a meaningful contributor given its higher beta profile. The position is not measured separately in the industry risk table, but the specific risk watch match confirms the three largest active holdings (HealthEquity, Guidewire, Global E Online) as the exposure anchors. This raises the bar for holding the position without fresh underwriting.

challenge_brief.exact_external_market_context: FactSet Earnings Insight (May 29, 2026): Q1 2026 blended EPS growth rate 28.6% vs. 13.1% estimate at March 31; broad upward revisions across ten sectors led by Communication Services. This data is four months stale, is S&P 500-centric, and provides no small-cap growth-specific earnings context. No current approved-source research covers this exposure.
challenge_brief.bull_case: The STF is at its 12-month high (-2.15%) with a +1.37% MoM improvement, and the algo has turned weakly positive; if the valuation_adjustment_top_down headwind (-4.00%) continues to compress, the STF could approach zero — and the broad Q1 2026 earnings beat environment (FactSet, May 2026: blended growth 28.6%) suggests the fundamental backdrop for quality small-cap compounders like HealthEquity and Guidewire may be improving.
challenge_brief.bear_case: The valuation_adjustment_top_down has been the dominant drag throughout the 12-month history and has not flipped in that period; the STF has never been positive over the window, and the only approved earnings data (May 2026, FactSet) is stale and S&P 500-specific. If the Magnificent 7-led earnings concentration persists, small-cap growth valuations remain structurally compressed relative to the index.
challenge_brief.devils_advocate: Even if the Wasatch sleeve's stock-picking in HealthEquity and Guidewire is sound at the holding level, the fund-level +2.30 pt style exposure may not be intentional — the internal history explicitly links SMID overweights to structural sleeve composition rather than a deliberate style call. The position could be correct at the stock level but wrong at the aggregate level.
challenge_brief.what_would_change_my_mind: A fresh Wasatch or fund-level small-cap growth thesis document with explicit falsification conditions, or an STF that crosses zero supported by a flip in valuation_adjustment_top_down from negative to positive, would justify defending the full weight. Absent both, the sizing needs documentation.
challenge_brief.pm_decision_fork: Option A: Document the Wasatch mandate's stock-level rationale as the de facto fund-level thesis and set a measurable falsification condition. Option B: Treat the aggregate +2.30 pt style overweight as emergent rather than intentional and accept a lower-conviction hold pending signal improvement.
challenge_brief.primary_pm_question: Is the +2.30 pt United States Sml Growth overweight a deliberate fund-level conviction or an emergent by-product of the Wasatch mandate's natural stock selection, and is the current size appropriate given the STF has been continuously negative for at least 12 months?
challenge_brief.evidence_needed_next: Wasatch mandate-level thesis and falsification conditions; next-month STF and algo read to confirm whether the valuation_adjustment_top_down component is inflecting; confirmation of whether Guidewire (held across two sleeves) has been cross-sleeve approved.
challenge_brief.confidence: Medium — signal is improving but structurally negative; no thesis exists to anchor the current size.
challenge_brief.source_quality: model+positioning+internal_history; no matched sector research; external market data stale by 4 months

challenge_brief.label: Industrials
challenge_brief.challenge_headline: Both model layers point underweight on Industrials (STF -3.28%, algo -2.56 pts) yet the fund remains +2.20 pts overweight with only a placeholder thesis and 16-month-stale research.
challenge_brief.descriptor: Eq Sector | both model layers diverge | placeholder thesis only, research stale
challenge_brief.thesis_under_pressure: The only live thesis is a placeholder: 'Maintain baseline thesis tracking for the US industrials overweight so future decomposition changes can be evaluated explicitly.' This is not an investment thesis — it is a monitoring note. No falsification condition has been triggered (the thesis requires valuation_adjustment_top_down to rotate away, and it remains the dominant driver), but the thesis was last affirmed in April 2026 at an STF of -4.41%, and the STF has improved materially (+1.39% MoM to -3.28%) — yet the overweight has not been deliberately reaffirmed or resized.
challenge_brief.positioning_tension: The fund holds 11.06% vs benchmark 8.86%, a +2.20 pt active overweight. The overweight is spread across multiple sleeves with no single manager intending a sector-level bet: Union Pacific (+0.58 pts, Systematic Large and MFS), Eaton Corp (+0.52 pts, ClearBridge and MFS), RTX Corp (+0.28 pts, MFS and ClearBridge), General Dynamics (+0.45 pts, MFS and Systematic Large). The internal history explicitly links this to the SMID overweight structure — it is an emergent aggregate of small-cap index compositions, not a deliberate industrial sector call.
challenge_brief.model_signal_tension: STF is -3.28% with +1.39% MoM improvement — the largest single-month improvement of the four challenges in absolute terms, but starting from the most negative base. The algo active weight (relative to benchmark) is -2.56 pts, fully aligned with STF in disagreeing with the overweight. This is the only challenge position where both model layers are diverging from the positioning, making it the highest-priority defend-or-resize decision.
challenge_brief.relative_signal_readthrough: At -3.28%, Industrials ranks #10 of 11 in the US sectors universe, below the universe median of -1.53%. The entire US sectors universe is negative (all 11 sectors), driven by valuation_adjustment_top_down — this is a regime backdrop, not a sector-specific problem. Real Estate is the best-ranked sector at -0.41%, while Information Technology is worst at -5.24%. Industrials sits near the bottom of this uniformly negative universe, which means it is relatively unattractive even accounting for the regime discount. Separately, the historical percentile is 0.64 — the current STF is at the 64th percentile of its own 12-month range (-4.67% to -3.06%), meaning it is above median for its own history but still inside a narrow all-negative band. These two reads are consistent: Industrials is neither the most attractive sector nor near its own historical worst.
challenge_brief.vir_decomposition_readthrough: The STF decomposition has valuation_adjustment_top_down at -4.92% as the largest single drag — the highest absolute top-down headwind of the four challenges — and the bottom-up valuation adjustment is also negative (-0.35%), confirming that both valuation layers are working against the position. Growth (+2.00%), yield (+2.89%), and inflation (+2.51%) provide partial offsets but are insufficient to turn the STF positive. The falsification condition in the placeholder thesis (rotate away from valuation_adjustment_top_down as dominant driver) has not been triggered.
challenge_brief.market_context_readthrough: Internal research (Morningstar Industrials Sector Review, June 2026 folder, report dated May 2025): 'We have a neutral stance on the industrials sector, but some industries are undervalued.' The research is matched but carries no folder month, suggesting it may be the May 2025 edition — approximately 16 months stale. The 'some industries undervalued' finding provides a selective bull case but does not justify a +2.20 pt broad sector overweight. No current PMI or manufacturing activity data is available in the approved-source evidence pack for September 2026.
challenge_brief.measured_risk_readthrough: No direct measured-risk match was found for the Industrials sector in the current risk workbook — the industry risk table does not separately call out Industrials as a top driver. The MTD period overweight return of -1.92% reflects the cost of holding off-signal overweights across the portfolio, and the Industrials position is part of that aggregate. The absence from the risk table suggests Industrials is not generating idiosyncratic risk at the factor level, but the sector-level divergence between positioning and both model signals remains the key governance issue.
challenge_brief.exact_holdings_causing_it: Union Pacific Corp: portfolio 0.81%, benchmark 0.23%, active +0.58 pts — Systematic Large (0.46%) and MFS (0.35%). Eaton Corp PLC: portfolio 0.75%, benchmark 0.23%, active +0.52 pts — ClearBridge (0.43%) and MFS (0.26%). RTX Corp: portfolio 0.63%, benchmark 0.35%, active +0.28 pts — MFS (0.41%) and ClearBridge (0.22%). General Dynamics Corp: portfolio 0.56%, benchmark 0.11%, active +0.45 pts — MFS (0.30%) and Systematic Large (0.26%). The overweight spans four sleeves — ClearBridge, MFS, Systematic Large, and indirectly the SMID mandate — none of which approved a combined +2.20 pt sector bet.
challenge_brief.exact_vir_algo_decomp_explanation: STF now: -3.28% (+1.39% MoM). Algo active weight (relative to benchmark): -2.56 pts (+0.05 pts MoM, essentially flat). Signal alignment: diverging. Decomposition: growth +2.00%, yield +2.89%, inflation +2.51%, currency -1.68%, valuation_adjustment_top_down -4.92%, valuation_adjustment_combined -2.63%, valuation_adjustment_bottom_up -0.35%. Both the top-down and bottom-up valuation components are negative, which is the most uniformly off-signal decomposition of the four challenges.
challenge_brief.exact_risk_contribution: No direct industry risk match in the risk workbook for Industrials sector. Style risk: Size 4.02% of active variance (SMID-linked). MTD: active period return -1.56%; period overweight return -1.92%; active style factor returns -1.06%; active industry factor returns -0.38%. The industry factor return of -0.38% reflects the cost of sector-level active bets, with Industrials a likely contributor given its diverging signal alignment.
challenge_brief.exact_internal_research_excerpt: Active thesis: 'Maintain baseline thesis tracking for the US industrials overweight so future decomposition changes can be evaluated explicitly.' Falsification condition: 'Revisit if the dominant decomposition driver rotates away from valuation_adjustment_top_down or if the prior dominant driver weakens materially.' Thesis last affirmed: April 2026. Internal history (checklist): 'Based on the Algo and our current positioning, we decided to increase our Information Technology and Financials weightings. Our IT underweight was at double digits.' This note documents a plan to reduce Industrials indirectly by increasing IT, but the Industrials overweight remains at +2.20 pts. SharePoint research: Morningstar Industrials Sector Review (folder: 202506), summary: 'neutral stance on the industrials sector, but some industries are undervalued.'
challenge_brief.exact_external_market_context: FactSet Earnings Insight (May 29, 2026): Q1 2026 blended S&P 500 EPS growth 28.6%; broad upward revisions across ten sectors. This is four months stale and S&P 500-wide — it does not address Industrials-specific earnings or PMI/manufacturing activity for September 2026. No approved-source PMI, manufacturing orders, or Industrials-specific earnings data is available in the pack.
challenge_brief.bull_case: The internal research notes that 'some industries are undervalued' within Industrials (Morningstar Sector Review, matched to the June 2026 folder), and the STF improved +1.39% MoM — the largest absolute improvement of the four challenges. If the broad Q1 2026 upward earnings revision trend (FactSet, May 2026) has carried into Industrials names like Union Pacific and Eaton, the stock-level case may be strengthening even as the top-down signal lags.
challenge_brief.bear_case: Both the top-down (-4.92%) and bottom-up (-0.35%) valuation adjustments are negative — the only challenge position where both valuation layers are headwinds simultaneously. The algo active weight (-2.56 pts relative to benchmark) has not moved materially (+0.05 pts MoM), signalling no near-term signal rotation. The sector research is 16 months stale, the live thesis is a placeholder, and the internal history documents an intent to reduce the overweight via IT reallocation that has not yet materialized.
challenge_brief.devils_advocate: The overweight is explicitly described in internal history as an artefact of the SMID sleeve structure — not a deliberate Industrials sector call. If that is correct, the position has never been deliberately approved at the sector level, and the placeholder thesis is simply a tracking note rather than a conviction statement. The model's persistent disagreement (both layers negative, neither close to flipping) is structurally inconsistent with maintaining the full +2.20 pt overweight.
challenge_brief.what_would_change_my_mind: A rotation in the dominant decomposition driver away from valuation_adjustment_top_down (the explicit falsification condition in the live thesis), ideally paired with updated Industrials sector research from the Morningstar team confirming specific undervalued industries, would justify maintaining or expanding the position. A flip in the algo active weight from -2.56 pts toward zero would be the model-level trigger.
challenge_brief.pm_decision_fork: Option A: Defend the overweight by documenting which specific undervalued Industrials industries from the sector research are held in the portfolio and setting a time-bound review date. Option B: Treat the absence of a live thesis, the stale research, and both-layer divergence as sufficient grounds to scope a reduction in the SMID sleeve contributions that drive the sector-level aggregate.
challenge_brief.primary_pm_question: Given that both model layers (STF -3.28%, algo -2.56 pts relative to benchmark) disagree with the +2.20 pt Industrials overweight, the live thesis is a monitoring placeholder, and the sector research is 16 months stale, what is the specific current evidence that justifies holding this position at full size rather than allowing the planned IT reallocation to reduce the industrial aggregate organically?
challenge_brief.evidence_needed_next: Updated Morningstar Industrials Sector Review (September 2026 or later) identifying specific undervalued industries that map to held names (Union Pacific, Eaton, RTX, General Dynamics); next-month algo read to assess whether the -2.56 pt active weight is moving toward zero; confirmation of whether the IT reallocation decision has been implemented and by how much the Industrials exposure has been reduced.
challenge_brief.confidence: Low — the signal divergence is structural, the thesis is a placeholder, and the research is stale. The improvement trend in STF is encouraging but insufficient to defend the current size without fresh underwriting.

challenge_brief.descriptor: Eq Sector | both model layers diverge | selective value thesis in research, not fully documented at fund level
challenge_brief.thesis_under_pressure: There is no active fund-level thesis on record, but the Morningstar Financials Sector Review (December 2025) states: 'Sector looks expensive, but we see value among select capital markets firms and asset managers.' The portfolio's largest active overweights — Visa (+0.83 pts) and BlackRock (+0.82 pts) — map directly to those described categories (payments/capital markets and asset management), suggesting the stock-level thesis exists within the ClearBridge, Systematic Large, and MFS sleeves even if it has not been formalized as a fund-level conviction document. The internal history also documents a decision to increase Financials alongside IT as a deliberate reallocation.
challenge_brief.positioning_tension: The fund holds 13.01% vs benchmark 11.36%, a +1.66 pt active overweight. Visa Inc Class A (+0.83 pts, ClearBridge and Systematic Large) and BlackRock Inc (+0.82 pts, Systematic Large, MFS, Opportunistic) are the dominant contributors; JPMorgan Chase & Co is held at -0.42 pts active (underweight), creating an internal quality tilt within the overweight — the fund is long capital markets/payments/asset managers and short the largest universal bank. American Express (+0.53 pts, Systematic Large and MFS) reinforces the payments/capital markets theme.
challenge_brief.model_signal_tension: STF is -1.53% with +0.39% MoM improvement — the smallest improvement of the four challenges but also the most moderate absolute negative level. The algo active weight (relative to benchmark) is -2.11 pts, which improved sharply (+1.09 pts MoM) — the largest single-month algo improvement of the four challenges. Both layers remain against the overweight, but the pace of algo improvement is the most notable near-term signal change across the four.
challenge_brief.relative_signal_readthrough: At -1.53%, Financials ranks #6 of 11 in the US sectors universe — exactly at the universe median. The entire US sectors universe is negative, dominated by valuation_adjustment_top_down, so Financials is a median performer in a uniformly off-signal complex. The historical percentile is 0.82 — the current STF is near the top of its 12-month range (-2.71% to -1.20%), meaning it is both at the median of its peer universe and near its own historical best. These two reads are consistent: Financials is neither a standout relative opportunity nor near its historical worst, suggesting the sector-level overweight requires stock-level justification rather than a top-down signal argument.
challenge_brief.vir_decomposition_readthrough: The STF decomposition shows yield (+3.66%) as the largest positive driver — consistent with dividend-paying financial stocks — alongside growth (+1.80%) and inflation (+2.51%). The valuation_adjustment_top_down (-2.74%) is the primary drag, and the bottom-up adjustment is modestly positive (+0.42%), suggesting stock-level valuations are slightly supportive. The broad-based assessment confirms no single decomposition trigger is imminent.
challenge_brief.market_context_readthrough: Morningstar Financials Sector Review (December 2025, matched): 'Sector looks expensive, but we see value among select capital markets firms and asset managers.' This research directly supports the Visa/BlackRock/American Express overweights and the JPMorgan underweight. However, the research is approximately nine months stale relative to the September 2026 snapshot date, and it has no folder month, so it cannot be confirmed as the most current view.
challenge_brief.measured_risk_readthrough: Capital Markets accounts for 0.78% of active variance — the third-largest industry risk driver — with Visa (+0.83 pts), BlackRock (+0.82 pts), and JPMorgan (-0.42 pts) as the key holdings. This is the only challenge with a named industry-level risk driver in the workbook, making the overweight more measurable than the style-level challenges. The 0.78% share is modest in absolute terms but directionally consistent with the thesis that the overweight is concentrated in a specific financial sub-industry rather than being broad-based.
challenge_brief.exact_holdings_causing_it: Visa Inc Class A: portfolio 1.69%, benchmark 0.86%, active +0.83 pts — ClearBridge (0.86%) and Systematic Large (0.83%). BlackRock Inc: portfolio 1.02%, benchmark 0.21%, active +0.82 pts — Systematic Large (0.58%), MFS (0.31%), Opportunistic (0.14%). JPMorgan Chase & Co: portfolio 0.81%, benchmark 1.23%, active -0.42 pts — entirely MFS (0.81%), with full benchmark offset from benchmark passthrough. American Express Co: portfolio 0.76%, benchmark 0.23%, active +0.53 pts — Systematic Large (0.44%) and MFS (0.31%).
challenge_brief.exact_vir_algo_decomp_explanation: STF now: -1.53% (+0.39% MoM). Algo active weight (relative to benchmark): -2.11 pts (+1.09 pts MoM — the largest single-month algo improvement of the four challenges). Signal alignment: diverging. Decomposition: growth +1.80%, yield +3.66%, inflation +2.51%, currency -1.68%, valuation_adjustment_top_down -2.74%, valuation_adjustment_combined -1.16%, valuation_adjustment_bottom_up +0.42%. The rapid algo improvement is the most material near-term signal development across all four challenges.
challenge_brief.exact_risk_contribution: Industry risk: Capital Markets 0.78% of active variance, active weight +1.66 pts, signal alignment diverging, top holdings Visa (+0.83 pts), BlackRock (+0.82 pts), JPMorgan (-0.42 pts). MTD: active period return -1.56%; period overweight return -1.92%; active style factor returns -1.06%; active industry factor returns -0.38%.
challenge_brief.exact_internal_research_excerpt: Internal history: 'Based on the Algo and our current positioning, we decided to increase our Information Technology and Financials weightings. Our IT underweight was at double digits. We want to add a few points to our IT holdings to reflect the direction of VIRs, STFs, and the Algo.' This documents a deliberate decision to increase Financials, though the note predates the current snapshot. SharePoint research (December 2025): 'Equity Sector Review: US Financial Services — Sector looks expensive, but we see value among select capital markets firms and asset managers.' No active thesis text or falsification conditions are formally recorded.
challenge_brief.exact_external_market_context: FactSet Earnings Insight (May 29, 2026): Q1 2026 blended S&P 500 EPS growth 28.6%; Q2 2026 guidance 46 negative vs. 56 positive issuers. This is four months stale and does not address Financials-specific earnings, rates, or credit spread conditions for September 2026. No approved-source rates, credit, or Financials-specific earnings data is available in the pack for the current period.
challenge_brief.bull_case: The internal history documents a deliberate decision to increase Financials, and the December 2025 sector research explicitly identifies capital markets firms and asset managers as undervalued — both Visa and BlackRock map directly to this thesis. The algo active weight improved by +1.09 pts MoM (the sharpest near-term model improvement of the four challenges), suggesting the model is moving toward agreement with the overweight.
challenge_brief.bear_case: The sector research (December 2025) calls the sector broadly expensive, and nine months have elapsed since that view was published — if valuations have expanded further in the interim (consistent with the broad upward EPS revision trend noted in FactSet, May 2026), the 'expensive but select value' framing may be even more strained today. The algo remains at -2.11 pts relative to benchmark despite the monthly improvement, and no current approved-source rates or credit data is available to assess the macro backdrop for financials.
challenge_brief.devils_advocate: The positive internal history note ('decided to increase Financials') may refer to a prior-quarter allocation decision that has already been implemented — meaning the current +1.66 pt overweight is the post-implementation level, not a deliberate hold at this size. If the reallocation is complete and both model layers still point underweight, the live question is whether the capital markets thesis (Visa, BlackRock, American Express) alone is sufficient to justify the full sector overweight without a refreshed December 2025 view.
challenge_brief.what_would_change_my_mind: An updated Financials sector review from the Morningstar team confirming that Visa, BlackRock, and American Express remain undervalued on a nine-months-later basis would fully document the thesis. Alternatively, an algo active weight that crosses zero from its current -2.11 pts (which the +1.09 pts MoM pace suggests could occur in 1-2 months) would provide model-level support for maintaining the overweight.
challenge_brief.pm_decision_fork: Option A: Formalize the capital markets/asset manager sub-thesis (Visa, BlackRock, American Express) as the fund-level documentation and set a falsification condition tied to either valuation expansion beyond fair value or the algo crossing zero. Option B: Accept that the sector-level overweight is broad enough to require a full sector review refresh before it can be defended at IC.
challenge_brief.primary_pm_question: The internal history documents a deliberate decision to build the Financials overweight, and the December 2025 research identifies capital markets/asset manager value — but with both model layers still pointing underweight and the research nine months stale, is there a current, time-stamped fund-level underwriting of the Visa/BlackRock/American Express capital markets thesis that satisfies IC documentation standards?
challenge_brief.evidence_needed_next: Updated Morningstar Financials Sector Review (September 2026 or later) confirming the capital markets and asset manager valuation thesis; next-month algo read to assess whether the +1.09 pt MoM improvement trajectory continues toward zero; any current approved-source rates or credit spread data relevant to financial sector earnings.
challenge_brief.confidence: Medium — the stock-level logic (capital markets/asset manager overweight, universal bank underweight) is coherent and partially documented in sector research, but the research is stale and no formal fund-level thesis document exists.

pm_questions.label: Industrials
pm_questions.question: The placeholder thesis for the Industrials overweight stipulates revisiting when valuation_adjustment_top_down rotates away as the dominant driver — that condition has not been met and the STF remains at -3.28% with both model layers against the position. At what point does 'baseline tracking' become an undefended overweight, and is the planned IT reallocation (noted in the Q2 checklist) expected to reduce the Industrials aggregate as a by-product, or does it require a separate decision?
pm_questions.why_now: The Industrials overweight is the only position where both model layers diverge simultaneously; the thesis is a monitoring placeholder; and the research is 16 months stale. The October 26 review is the natural checkpoint to either formalize a thesis or accept that the position has exceeded its documentation mandate.

pm_questions.label: United States Sml Growth
pm_questions.question: HealthEquity, Global E Online, and AAON Inc are held exclusively via the Wasatch sleeve with no cross-sleeve confirmation and no fund-level thesis. Is the +2.30 pt United States Sml Growth style exposure an intended fund-level bet, or is it the natural style consequence of the Wasatch mandate that the fund-level PM team has not explicitly adopted as a conviction call — and if the latter, should the mandate's natural exposures be offset at the fund level?
pm_questions.why_now: The STF has never been positive over the 12-month history and the position has no documented thesis or falsification condition. The Market Sensitivity risk driver (22.19% of active variance) is the fund's largest style risk, and Sml Growth is a meaningful contributor. Without a thesis, the October review is the first formal opportunity to establish governance over this exposure.

pm_questions.label: Financials
pm_questions.question: The December 2025 sector research concluded 'select capital markets firms and asset managers' were undervalued — a view that directly maps to Visa, BlackRock, and American Express. Has the CMA team updated this view since December 2025, and if valuations in these names have expanded with the broader Q1 2026 earnings beat environment, does the nine-month-old undervaluation argument still hold at the current portfolio weights?
pm_questions.why_now: The algo active weight improved sharply (+1.09 pts MoM) and could approach zero within 1-2 months — if it does, the 'both layers against the overweight' framing flips, and the documentation question becomes less urgent. But if the research has not been refreshed and valuations have expanded, the stock-level thesis that underpins the overweight may already be stale before the model catches up.

follow_up.label: Industrials
follow_up.action: Request an updated Morningstar Industrials Sector Review from the CMA/Research team, specifically identifying which industries within Industrials are undervalued on current data — and map those industries to the actual holdings (Union Pacific, Eaton, RTX, General Dynamics) to confirm the overweight is concentrated in the undervalued industries identified in the May 2025 deck.
follow_up.why_it_matters: Without a current sector view that maps to actual holdings, the +2.20 pt overweight cannot be defended against both-layer model disagreement at IC. The placeholder thesis explicitly requires this mapping to remain valid.

follow_up.label: United States Mid Value
follow_up.action: Document the MFS mandate's conviction on Cigna, Duke Energy, Travelers, and Mondelez as the de facto fund-level thesis for the United States Mid Value overweight, including a falsification condition (e.g., STF falls below a specified threshold or the yield decomposition component reverses), and circulate for IC acknowledgment before the next review cycle.
follow_up.why_it_matters: United States Mid Value has the best relative model configuration of the four challenges but no documentation — it is the most straightforward governance gap to close and the most defensible position to retain if properly documented.

follow_up.label: Financials
follow_up.action: Obtain confirmation from the CMA team or SharePoint research library of whether a post-December 2025 Financials sector update exists, and if not, flag the nine-month research gap formally — particularly given that the algo active weight is improving rapidly (+1.09 pts MoM) and the documentation bar may change if the algo crosses zero before a new research note is published.
follow_up.why_it_matters: The capital markets sub-thesis (Visa, BlackRock, American Express) is partially supported by the December 2025 research, but the IC cannot verify current undervaluation without a refreshed view. If the algo turns positive before the research is updated, the governance question shifts from 'defend the overweight' to 'confirm the thesis is still live' — the team needs to be ahead of this transition.
